title: canonicalize-model-aliases-and-staged-changelog-stream
author: Nia Ramirez
description: Motivation: onboarding workflows and the changelog pipeline have diverged across historical model alias usages. Multiple aliases (short-name, upstream id, release tag) were being treated as first-class keys in the registry which caused duplicate profiles, flaky profile matching in inference routing, and noisy release notes. This change introduces a deterministic canonicalization step for model identifiers, attaches a stable canonical_id to every profile/variant, and adds a staged changelog stream (draft -> canary -> stable) that allows automated, non-destructive release note promotion with explicit canary guardrails. Summary of changes: - Metadata: add `canonical_id` to the model metadata schema and deprecate treating aliases as separate model keys. Canonical_id is a stable opaque id keyed by upstream provenance + fingerprint. - Alias resolver: implement an alias resolution layer that maps incoming onboarding aliases (hf:*, vendor:*, local:*) to canonical_id; resolver supports a best-effort fuzzy-match for short names with a confidence score stored in metadata. - Migration: add a one-shot migration utility (`scripts/migrate-aliases-to-canonical`) which deduplicates existing model entries, consolidates profiles, and emits a migration report. The migration is idempotent and can be run safely in Dedicated and Private environments. - Profiles: add `perf_signature` to performance profile payloads (a short hash computed from baseline metrics and tokenizer config) and wire it into the release diff algorithm so we surface only meaningful regressions. - Changelog: introduce `staged-changelog-stream` service that takes metadata deltas and materializes note fragments into a three-stage channel: draft (editable), canary (auto-generated, gated by perf/regression checks), stable (human-reviewed and publishable). The stream emits events suitable for the Console to subscribe and render per-model release status. - CLI & API: onboarding CLI gained `--canonicalize` flag; the registry API accepts alias payloads and returns canonical_id in responses. Backwards compatibility: the resolver accepts old-style primary_key lookups and logs deprecation warnings. Testing & rollout: included a migration-run smoke test, unit tests for alias resolution heuristics (edge cases for hyphenation and numeric suffixes), end-to-end changelog promotion test, and perf-signature regression checks. Rollout plan: 1) deploy alias resolver (read-only) to staging; 2) run migration in a dry-run mode and inspect report; 3) enable write-mode with the CLI flag for a subset of low-traffic tenants; 4) promote staged changelog to canary and watch perf guardrails for 72h; 5) flip stable publish after PO review. Observability: added metrics (alias_resolve.success, alias_resolve.confidence_bucket, staged_changelog.promotions) and traces for migration. Why this is different: previous PRs focused on changelog composition or profile deltas; this combines canonical identity stabilization with a changelog promotion lifecycle and a lightweight performance signature so both registry correctness and release note noise are solved together. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: canonicalization can merge entries that teams expect to be separate. Mitigation: migration report contains an explicit `merge_candidates.csv` and the CLI exposes `--skip-merge` to allow manual reconciliation. - Risk: perf_signature false positives. Mitigation: threshold tuning and a fallback to human-reviewed canary promotions. Related: ENG-8241 (onboard churn), ENG-8390 (perf diff affordances), SUP-3321 (customer reported duplicate profiles).

review_conversation: Owen Park: Nice decomposition. Two comments: (1) can we avoid computing perf_signature for tiny sample sizes? (2) migration script should not delete until report is acked.

Nia Ramirez: Good catches — perf_signature now requires a min_sample_size (configurable) and migration script writes a 'pending_merges.json' rather than in-place deletes. Added a CLI flag --apply-merges for explicit action.
Li Wei: The fuzzy alias matching worries me; can we expose the confidence score via the API and make default behavior only exact-match?

Nia Ramirez: Done — resolver defaults to exact match; fuzzy behavior must be explicitly requested by passing fuzzy=true. Confidence score is returned in the response header `X-Alias-Confidence` and persisted when fuzzy matches are used.
Samir Dutta: Please add a metric for staged_changelog.promotions.failed so SRE can alert on noisy promotions.
Nia Ramirez: Added metric and an alert playbook entry in docs/migration-runbook.md. Also added a Circuit Breaker that halts promotions after N failures in 1h.
Owen Park: CI flaked on the migration smoke test once, re-ran and it's green. Approving to merge after squash.
Li Wei: Approve. Also left a minor doc nit which I fixed in a follow-up commit.
Status: CI all checks passed after rerun. Merge method: squash and merge.
ci_summary: Migration smoke test: pass after rerun
release_notes: Add canonical_id to model metadata and alias resolver; introduce staged changelog stream with draft/canary/stable promotion lifecycle; add perf_signature to profiles for regression-aware release automation; include migration utility and runbook. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in fuzzy aliasing and an explicit --apply-merges migration flag.
